storylines.title: France riots and European unrest
storylines.summary: French cost-of-living protests continue into a sixth week: over 140,000 rallied Saturday, with tear gas in Paris and Lyon and arrests of Yellow Vests who defied a ban. Budget talks are deadlocked; Thursday's strike drew about 600,000, per the interior ministry.

events.text: More than 140,000 rally across France; tear gas is fired in Paris and Lyon and Yellow Vests defying a ban are arrested.
Unions stage a general strike; the interior ministry estimates 600,000 marchers nationwide, with unions citing a far higher number.
France braces for a nationwide strike and marches over cost of living and education as parliamentary budget talks remain deadlocked.
France opens an attempted-murder investigation after petrol bombs are thrown at riot police at Saturday's protests; no arrests reported.
Germany's cost-of-living protests turn violent in Berlin, Hamburg and Frankfurt, with shops looted, the same day hundreds of thousands protest in France.
Police clash with masked rioters in Paris, Marseille and other cities after largely peaceful third-wave marches across France.
Macron bans 'illegitimate' protests; total ban in Marseille and Lyon, union-organised marches only elsewhere, museums closed Saturday.
France's 10-year borrowing costs reach 5% for the first time since 2002, the FT reports.
Macron accuses Trump and other foreign leaders of 'stupid comments' about the unrest as France readies for more protests this weekend.
France announces nightly curfews in Paris, Lyon and other cities for as long as necessary after the first quiet night.
EU regulators probe pro-Kremlin disinformation and the role of social platforms around the French riots, the FT reports.
Italy approves sending 500 troops to Milan after clashes and protests.

storylines.title: US-Ukraine rift over Starlink and strikes
storylines.summary: US-mediated trilateral talks opened in Abu Dhabi with Europe attending; the first day lasted nearly four hours and Zelensky called it constructive. Talks resume Wednesday. Zelenskyy warns Russia aims to cut Ukraine in half; Russia rations petrol.

events.text: First day of Abu Dhabi talks lasts nearly four hours; Zelensky calls it constructive and talks are expected to resume Wednesday, BBC and NPR report.
US officials say they will seek a 'final end' to the war at Abu Dhabi talks, including a security-architecture proposal; the FT says expectations are low.
BBC: Kyiv, Washington and Moscow send delegations to the UAE; US officials cite 'some flexibility' by both sides.
Zelenskyy warns Russian strikes on Dnipro bridges aim to cut Ukraine in half, the FT reports.
White House says it is cautiously optimistic about Abu Dhabi talks on Tuesday and Wednesday, the first with US mediators since February, Axios reports.
Rosneft limits petrol sales after new Ukrainian refinery strikes, the FT reports.
Trump tells '60 Minutes' that 'hatred' between Zelensky and Putin is a main obstacle to ending the war, The Hill reports.
France says European officials will attend the Abu Dhabi talks, the first three-way round since February, defying Kremlin objections, NPR reports.
Russia strikes Kyiv's energy grid with 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles, causing blackouts and water shortages, The Guardian reports.
Britain and France will lead 2,800 troops from 11 nations in a Poland exercise for a postwar Ukraine deployment, Defense News reports.
Russia fires missiles at Kyiv, damaging buildings and injuring two civilians after Zelenskyy warned of new attacks, Al Jazeera reports.
Al Jazeera reports Russia's territorial gains are dwindling and US traders reportedly refuse to honor Trump's diesel deal with Putin.
Trump says a Russia-Ukraine deal is 'very close' after meeting Putin's envoy, giving no specifics; he did not meet the Ukrainian delegation.
Melania Trump hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials at the White House and urges them to build on the recent local truce.
Zelenskyy says he spoke for 90 minutes with Witkoff and Kushner ahead of trilateral talks; he and EU officials hope a Democratic Congress will help.
Kyiv says bodycam video shows a double-tap Russian strike on Komyshuvakha; at least 40 are dead and about 30 may be under rubble.
Zelenskyy says 40 are confirmed dead after a Russian strike on a school in Komyshuvakha; Kyiv releases bodycam video.
Russian and Ukrainian delegations are to meet Melania Trump at the White House Thursday after the Oleshky ceasefire.
Russian attacks on an aid centre, hospice and hospital kill at least 38 in 24 hours; Zelenskyy says dozens may be trapped.

storylines.title: AI debt worries and market selloff
storylines.summary: After Democrats won Congress, AI stocks plunged; Monday brought the best day in seven months. SoftBank posted a $7 billion loss. Anthropic set an IPO range of $70-$78 a share, implying up to $1.4 trillion, with pricing expected Nov. 18.

events.text: Anthropic sets an IPO range of $70 to $78 a share, implying a valuation up to $1.404 trillion; trading is expected Nov. 19.
SoftBank swings to a roughly $7 billion quarterly net loss, its first in nearly two years, as its share price has halved, the FT reports.
Anthropic is expected to set its IPO valuation range this week, the WSJ reported, per TechCrunch.
MarketWatch: the Dow has its third 1,000-point swing in four days, and volatility may not be over.
US stocks post their best day in seven months as tech rallies and oil slumps, while Nvidia falls, Bloomberg reports.
Anthropic can begin formally marketing its IPO as early as Tuesday, Bloomberg reports, after releasing new models.
Goldman CEO Solomon says AI financing remains strong despite market jitters; CoreWeave and Nebius have lost about half their value in a month.
Alphabet has discussed its first Hong Kong and Singapore dollar bonds, Bloomberg reports, a test of Asian appetite after the AI selloff.
Asian stocks rebound after last week's AI-driven rout pushed many indices into bear market territory, the FT reports.
Bloomberg says Meta's roughly $25 billion bond sale, launched on Election Day, highlights a shifting landscape for tech debt.
Bloomberg says Wall Street strategists call the post-election rout a fresh reason to buy; the FT says hedge funds and retail investors fled the AI trade.
Al Jazeera reports voters rejected data center development in all but one of 41 ballot measures in Tuesday's midterms.
Crusoe sells a troubled Wyoming data center project to Google, TechCrunch reports.
Democrats and Sen. Bernie Sanders renew calls for data center moratoriums after the midterms, the Guardian reports.
FT says Anthropic will press ahead with an IPO before Thanksgiving; CNBC says investors expect a valuation below $1.5 trillion.
OpenAI reportedly raises an additional $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation in a round not yet closed, TechCrunch reports.
US stocks rebound, with the Nasdaq 100 up over 1% in afternoon trading as chipmakers recover; options volume hit a record Thursday.
Microsoft winds down the number of neocloud partners as the AI buildout shows signs of strain, CNBC reports.
OpenAI's CFO tells CNBC the company will keep investing in data centers despite election results.
Japan's Nikkei 225 enters a technical bear market and Seoul's Kospi falls below 5,000 as the AI selloff deepens in Asia, Bloomberg reports.

storylines.title: Fed under Warsh weighs further hikes
storylines.summary: After a September hike, the Fed held in October. October CPI rose 0.4%, above forecasts, and Treasuries sold off. Governor Waller floated a 50bp hike. Kalshi puts a December 25bp hike at 85%. October payrolls rose 165,000; unemployment is 4.1%.

events.text: Governor Waller says policymakers should weigh a 50bp hike if inflation fails to slow, the FT reports.
October consumer prices rise 0.4%, more than expected; Treasury yields jump as December hike bets firm, CNBC and Bloomberg report.
Chicago Fed's Goolsbee says the AI data center buildout is overheating the economy and putting upward pressure on prices.
October CPI is due Tuesday, expected at +0.3% headline and +0.2% core, CNBC reports.
Bloomberg Economics' Anna Wong says the broad-based jobs gain strengthens the case for another Fed rate hike in December.
US adds 165,000 jobs in October and unemployment slips to 4.1%; Treasuries fall as bets on a December Fed hike strengthen.
ADP says private employers added 86,000 jobs in October, slightly above expectations.
Axios reports Trump's effort to replace Fed governors with allies looks dead now that Democrats control the Senate.
September job openings rise to 7.52 million, above the 7.15 million consensus, ahead of the payrolls report.
NPR: GDP growth is up but so are prices; interest rates are staying the same for now, with midterms ahead.
Axios: traders bet oil prices stay elevated longer, threatening to prolong inflation pressure.
CNBC reports housing data worsened in September as the Fed weighs more rate hikes; Axios says homebuilder sentiment is at a 14-year low.
MarketWatch says the October decision is a closer call than markets think, weighing arguments against a hike.
Warsh says the economy has performed largely as expected since the September hike; markets expect a hold.

storylines.title: 2026 midterm elections
storylines.summary: Democrats won the House, Senate and most governorships. House Republicans elected Jim Jordan minority leader; Senate Republicans paused leadership elections. Hegseth calls Massie's impeachment push a farce as a House vote nears; Miller is chief of staff.

events.text: House Republicans elect Jim Jordan minority leader over Steve Scalise, 106-73; Tom Emmer remains whip.
Senate Republicans pause their leadership elections after a closed-door meeting where conservatives pressed Majority Leader Thune, The Hill reports.
Hegseth calls the impeachment effort a 'farce' at his first briefing since May; Vance says the vote 'isn't about Iran.'
Massie says there is a 'high probability' Hegseth won't last the year; Trump says Hegseth should be praised, not impeached.
Speaker Mike Johnson declines to commit to serving in the next Congress, the Washington Examiner reports.
Seven GOP senators now seek a delay of leadership elections; Thune is still expected to be reelected, Axios reports.
Trump says he will stand by Hegseth as Massie forces a House impeachment vote later this week.
Rep. Thomas Massie files articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Hegseth; a House vote could come this week, NPR reports.
Trump questions midterm integrity on Truth Social without evidence, the BBC reports; Schumer criticizes the claims.
Trump tells DHS chief Mullin to engage Democrats on immigration but rules out amnesty, Fox reports; Jeffries says Democrats won't fund deportations.
Sullivan campaign moves to intervene against Peltola's ballot-records lawsuit in Alaska, The Hill reports.
House Ways and Means Chair Jason Smith urges delaying Tuesday's GOP leadership election, The Hill reports.
Trump tells '60 Minutes' his deportation policy 'might be too tough' and helped and hurt Republicans, and offers Democrats an immigration deal, The Hill reports.
Attorney General Todd Blanche backs Trump's call for a DOJ probe of Democrats' impeachment threats and declines to rule out prosecuting lawmakers, Axios reports.
Trump asks the Justice Department to investigate Democrats, including Sen. Elissa Slotkin, over what he calls 'extortion' in impeachment threats against officials.
Democrat Chris Mann is projected to unseat Kansas Attorney General Kris Kobach, per the AP.
Stephen Miller pledges 'absolute loyalty' to Trump at a Mar-a-Lago event; Fox reports House Republicans reacted angrily to the promotion.
Mary Peltola's campaign sues Alaska for records of rejected absentee ballots in the uncalled Senate race.
Sen. Thom Tillis says Stephen Miller is the 'worst of all possible choices' for chief of staff and Trump needs to rethink it.

storylines.title: US-Iran war and oil prices
storylines.summary: Trump calls the war effectively over; Rubio says no need for further major combat operations. Iran dismisses this and demands US acceptance of its conditions. Oil fell below $90. A Reuters/Ipsos poll finds 71% want Congress to end the war. Saudi Arabia reports pipeline attacks.

events.text: Oil falls below $90 as Trump pulls back from threat to strike Iran; Rubio says there is no need for major combat operations.
Reuters/Ipsos poll finds 71% of Americans want Congress to pass legislation ending the conflict with Iran.
US reportedly evacuated aircraft from RAF Mildenhall after an Iranian threat, the WSJ reported, per the Guardian.
Saudi forces intercept two missiles fired at Riyadh after reporting damage to the East-West pipeline, Al Jazeera reports.
Iranian officials dismiss Trump's 'effectively over' remarks as fake news and demand the US accept Iran's conditions, Al Jazeera reports.
Trump hails 'positive momentum' toward ending the war after calls with regional leaders, the FT reports.
Trump calls the Iran war 'effectively over' and new attacks 'quite unlikely' after meeting Qatar's prime minister, Al Jazeera and Axios report.
Saudi Arabia reports a new attack on its East-West pipeline, which bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, Al Jazeera reports.
France blames Iran's Revolutionary Guards for cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration, the Guardian reports.
Oil extends its biggest weekly drop since April 2020 as traders weigh diplomacy against fresh attacks, Bloomberg reports.
Rubio calls the Iran war unpopular but necessary and Tehran's negotiating demands 'outrageous and ridiculous,' Al Jazeera reports.
Iran's foreign minister gives the US two days to accept Tehran's offer or face escalation; Trump says renewed strikes are 'highly unlikely' if talks progress.
US launches a task force to stop Iran moving weapons and materials over land routes; Iranian media report blasts on Qeshm and in Bandar Abbas.
CENTCOM says it disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman after its crew ignored repeated warnings.
Iran's IRGC says it is building underground sites for weapons production and storage so missile output can continue under bombardment.
The Guardian reports Qatar is urging Iran to admit UN inspectors to bombed nuclear sites, possibly tied to reopening Hormuz.
Trump confirms a new round of limited strikes on an Iranian air defense system at Qeshm island and claims 'a lot of progress' in talks.
Axios, citing two sources, reports Vance has been personally involved for two weeks in indirect talks with Iran on a ceasefire and nuclear negotiations.
Oil swings as traders weigh diplomatic efforts to de-escalate the Iran war, Bloomberg reports.
Fox News reports Russian documents show a contract for 90 precision-guided missile launchers destined for Iran before the war.

storylines.title: Binance $6.3 billion hack
storylines.summary: Binance says suspected North Korean hackers used fake job interviews and a tampered installer to steal $6.3 billion, and that 98% of affected assets are replenished. North Korea denies involvement. The CFO is now leaving to pursue a new venture.

events.text: Binance's CFO is leaving to 'pursue a new venture' barely more than a week after the hack, TechCrunch reports.
Binance says the hackers spent months planning, using laptop infections, compromised internal tooling and fake job interviews.
North Korea fires multiple missiles and Kim Yo Jong rejects dialogue with the US while denying responsibility for the hack.
Binance's postmortem says hackers used fake job interviews and an internal AI tool; it says 98% of affected assets are replenished.
North Korea denies being behind the hack; the FT reports hackers are expected to take months to launder the funds.
Binance users withdraw $3.6 billion after the exchange resumes transactions following the largest-ever crypto hack, the BBC reports.
Binance resumes phased withdrawals; TechCrunch reports 95% of stolen assets covered, while Binance's own figure reported elsewhere is 90%.
Binance says 90% of losses are covered and withdrawals resume Sunday; FBI says North Korea-backed TraderTraitor is behind the attack.

storylines.title: Israel election deadlock
storylines.summary: President Herzog tasked Gadi Eisenkot with forming a government, giving him 28 days to reach 61 Knesset seats; Netanyahu claims the vote was stolen, though Shin Bet found no foreign interference. The new Knesset was sworn in Tuesday.

events.text: New Knesset is sworn in Tuesday, giving opposition a chance at some levers of power; Shin Bet reportedly finds no foreign election interference.
Foreign Policy says Eisenkot has four paths to a coalition, none easy.
Eisenkot starts coalition talks, reaching out to Netanyahu allies and warning Israel nears a 'point of no return,' the Guardian reports.
Herzog gives Gadi Eisenkot 28 days to form a government, passing over Netanyahu after the deadlocked Oct. 27 election.
The Guardian reports the Democratic midterm sweep may help Israel's splintered opposition unite to unseat Netanyahu, a close Trump ally.
Al Jazeera says Eisenkot's bloc and Arab-led parties seek to oust Netanyahu, but failure to form a government could leave him in power.
Herzog says he will name a candidate on Sunday after a majority of lawmakers endorse Eisenkot over Netanyahu, Al Jazeera reports.
Arab parties led by Yousef Jabareen tell Herzog they back Gadi Eisenkot over Netanyahu to form a government.
Herzog accepts the vote results and opens talks on forming a government, a blow to Netanyahu's efforts to discredit the election, Al Jazeera reports.
President Herzog begins consultations with parties and warns not every promise can be fulfilled if they want to avoid another election.
Israel's election body says the deadlocked result will stand even if foreign-interference claims are proven, as Netanyahu alleges the election was 'stolen'.
Arab coalition leader Yousef Jabareen says he is ready to join the opposition bloc to oust Netanyahu after record seat gains, the Guardian reports.

storylines.title: Nvidia CEO Huang spy scandal
storylines.summary: Nvidia's board is investigating CEO Jensen Huang over his affair with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy tied to Megaspeed, and has hired Wachtell Lipton to lead the probe. Trump says the FBI is looking into it; shareholders have sued.

events.text: Nvidia hires law firm Wachtell Lipton, including a former acting SDNY US attorney, to lead the probe of Huang's affair, CNBC and the FT report.
Shareholders sue Nvidia and Huang, accusing them of defrauding investors over the affair with an alleged Chinese spy, the Guardian reports.
Trump says the FBI is looking into Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy and that he believes Huang did not know of her work, the BBC reports.
CNBC profiles Megaspeed, the Singapore-based Nvidia chip buyer previously probed over alleged chip supplies to China.
